subsystems.name: Quantum entropy source
subsystems.role: generates raw random bits from inherently unpredictable quantum events.
parts: attenuated laser or spontaneous parametric down-conversion source

subsystems.name: Single-photon detection
subsystems.role: measures photon states to extract randomness and detect eavesdropping.
parts: superconducting nanowire detectors for higher performance

subsystems.name: Key processing unit
subsystems.role: runs the key-exchange protocol and turns raw bits into secure keys.

subsystems.name: Secure key storage
subsystems.role: holds generated keys where they cannot be read or copied.

subsystems.name: Quantum and classical interfaces
subsystems.role: connects to a peer for quantum transmission and classical reconciliation.
parts: USB or Bluetooth for classical channel

subsystems.name: Tamper protection
subsystems.role: detects physical intrusion and erases keys instantly.

subsystems.name: Power and enclosure
subsystems.role: makes the device portable and usable.

buildSteps.title: Design the photonic chip
buildSteps.detail: Lay out waveguides, splitters and modulators on a silicon photonics platform to route single photons with minimal loss.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate source and detectors
buildSteps.detail: Integrate a compact photon source and single-photon detectors on or beside the chip, using SPADs for a handheld form factor.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the quantum random number generator
buildSteps.detail: Measure quantum noise such as photon arrival time or vacuum fluctuations, digitize it, and produce raw random bits.

buildSteps.title: Implement the key-exchange protocol
buildSteps.detail: Program the processor to run BB84: choose bases, sift, correct errors, and apply privacy amplification to distill a secret key.

buildSteps.title: Build secure storage and tamper layer
buildSteps.detail: Embed the processor and memory in a tamper-responsive enclosure that zeroizes keys on intrusion.

buildSteps.title: Integrate interfaces and power
buildSteps.detail: Add an optical port for the quantum channel, a USB or Bluetooth link for classical messages, and a battery with a simple user interface.

buildSteps.title: Test and certify
buildSteps.detail: Verify randomness with statistical test suites, measure key rate and quantum bit error rate, and validate resistance to side-channel attacks.

prerequisites.why: commercial detectors exist, but chip-scale versions efficient enough for a key-fob are still maturing.
commercial QRNG chips already produce certified randomness from quantum processes.
deployed in metro networks and dedicated links, but not yet at mass scale or in consumer devices.
silicon photonics can guide and manipulate photons, but loss and detector integration remain challenges.
hardware security modules already protect keys in payment and government systems.

pathway.milestone: QRNG chips in servers and QKD links between data centers
pathway.unlocks: quantum-safe key exchange for high-value fixed links.

pathway.milestone: chip-scale QKD endpoints integrated into network equipment
pathway.unlocks: lower cost and smaller footprint for metro and campus networks.

pathway.milestone: hybrid devices combining QKD with post-quantum cryptography
pathway.unlocks: defense in depth if either method is later compromised.

pathway.milestone: portable quantum-safe communication devices for field use
pathway.unlocks: secure links for mobile users and remote infrastructure.
